summary: A bare developer page for an experimental fractal bitmap typeface: letters are PNGs generated by a PHP library, not a webfont. The whole page is the same 146-glyph table repeated at growing recursion depths, so scrolling makes the alphabet visibly zoom into itself; install and usage snippets follow.

instances.look: A small blue fractal ×5 logo beside four short paragraphs of default-looking text, with no display treatment: the block stands in for a hero and intro
instances.ux: Logo links home; inline links to ACJ and the Royal Academy of Arts
instances.learn: Let a tiny self-similar logo image do the display work beside a README-style lead when the type itself is the page's only design

reconstruction.layout: Full-width band 240px tall; logo 125×125 PNG scaled to ~230px at top-left; text runs from x≈230 to the right margin; first-line indents on later paragraphs
reconstruction.typography: System sans (-apple-system) 16px, leading ~1.3, black; links blue, the RA link magenta
reconstruction.content: '×5 (pronounced Times Five) is an experimental typeface, based on a 5 by 5 (pixel) grid/matrix that repeats itself…' and the red/blue glyph groups explained

instances.look: The same 146-glyph table three times under dark labelled bars: 'Base' as a tiny pixel strip, 'Second power' as a compact grid, 'Third power' as huge 6-column cells where each stroke is itself a smaller pattern. Black for Unicode glyphs, red for non-standard ones, blue for algorithmic ones
instances.ux: Each cell is a link with the Unicode name in its title, going to a per-glyph page (/u0041). Section bars stick to the top while scrolling; a ▲ button returns to the top
instances.learn: For a generative typeface, repeat the entire table at increasing recursion depth: the same order at each scale turns a character map into a demonstration of how the design works

reconstruction.layout: Three stacked sections, each a full-width wrapping flex grid of 146 hairline cells: n1 ~20px cells in 2 rows, 89px tall; n2 ~50px cells in 6 rows, 349px tall; n3 ~215px cells, 6 columns with a grey gutter at right, 5280px tall. Dark 40px section bars on top of each
reconstruction.typography: Glyphs are pixel PNGs (5ⁿ px per side, shown at 2×, image-rendering crisp); section titles 14–16px system sans, white on #404040
reconstruction.behaviour: Sticky section headers (they repeat in the stitched crop); images lazy-load, so cells fill in as they enter the viewport (t≈1–3s in the video); cells are plain links
reconstruction.content: All glyphs in Unicode order: Latin, numerals, punctuation, geometric shapes, then red ligatures and monograms, then blue fractal constructions
reconstruction.html: a[href=/u0041][title='Latin Capital Letter A'] > img.n2 (146 per section); class n1, n2, n3 sets the display size

instances.look: 'Higher powers' section with a two-item bullet list linking to the separate pages /n4 and /n5, which are too large to inline; thin dark section bar

README-style 'Installation' and 'Usage' sections: code boxes for 'composer require acj/x5' and 'git clone …', then HTML and PHP snippets with a blue left border. The stitched crop of 05 is overlaid by the fixed header
instances.ux: Copy the commands by hand; no download button. Glyphs can also be hot-linked straight from their image URL
instances.learn: When the typeface is a library, its install commands and an image URL scheme (size, codepoint, transparency flag) are the checkout

reconstruction.layout: Installation: two side-by-side columns with a heading and a code block each, 114px tall; Usage: same two columns ~210px tall, with a paragraph under the HTML column
reconstruction.typography: Headings 16px system sans; code 14px Consolas/monospace with syntax colours; bars 14px white on #404040

instances.look: 'Applications': one square image of the designer's logo built from coloured dots and ×5 patterns on near-black, with two bullet lists of links to his logo, personal and design-system projects
instances.feel: Colourful break in a mono page
instances.learn: A single colour application at the end proves that a dry black-and-white system can generate something rich
